summary: Open continuity event streams without following filesystem links

delivery.outcome: Reject linked/non-regular continuity stream targets before reading or writing. Use anchored POSIX directory descriptors and held Windows no-delete-sharing no-follow handles. Preserve append-only replay/recovery and absence behavior; publish immutable standard 0.20.73.
nonGoals: Change event/index schema, history or execution/publication authority
Introduce a runtime dependency or bundled continuity module
Claim protection against arbitrary same-user concurrent changes beyond verified descriptor/path boundaries
Mutate foreign or frozen target work

architecture.decision: Use one private stream descriptor context in the existing standalone continuity module for append and iteration. POSIX opens each directory segment relative to a no-follow directory descriptor. Windows holds no-follow directory handles without delete sharing and checks reparse attributes before opening the single-linked regular file. No pathname-based data writes or platform fallback that follows links. Existing OS-owned transaction and index replacement remain unchanged.
interfaceChanges: Existing continuity read/append functions reject unsafe link/non-regular targets with structured continuity errors.
architecture.rollback: Revert the material source fix through protected publication; preserve controller and review receipts.

validation.evidence: Actual file/parent symlink and hardlink attacks reproduce foreign mutation; regressions check unchanged targets, descriptor substitution, no-follow capability boundary, real append/read and replay/concurrency.
Native gate, existing continuity/integration/wheel and exact-head Linux/Windows/OneDev checks pass.
Independent protected merge and final standard v0.20.73 release verified.
